hook: You sleep eight hours and wake up exhausted — every single day
topic: Sleep duration vs. sleep architecture — why hours are the wrong metric
body:
**You're sleeping eight hours. You wake up exhausted. You've ruled out sleep as the problem. And that is exactly the wrong conclusion.**

Sleep duration is a poor proxy for sleep quality. What determines how your brain performs the next day is not how many hours you logged — it is the architecture of those hours. Specifically: how much slow-wave deep sleep you achieved, and whether your REM cycles were complete.

Deep sleep is when the glymphatic system runs its waste clearance. REM is when the brain consolidates memory, processes emotional load, and recalibrates neurotransmitter balance.

An eight-hour night with fragmented deep sleep — caused by alcohol, late-night screens, irregular sleep timing, or elevated cortisol — can produce worse cognitive outcomes the next day than six hours of high-quality, architecturally intact sleep.

You are not sleeping enough. You are sleeping the wrong kind of sleep.

Duration is easy to measure. Architecture is what matters. And several of the factors degrading yours are correctable within this week.
